title: Matrix Rust SDK replacement security threat model

in_scope: encrypted SDK stores and native secret stores
Matrix media retrieval, decryption, caching, and delivery
diagnostics, errors, logs, and support exports
shutdown, logout, wipe, crash, and partial failure
filesystem confinement, symlinks, and account isolation
migration, cutover, cleanup, rollback, widgets, and calls
proxy configuration, dependencies, CI, packaging, and supported platforms
non_goals: Protecting secrets after full root or kernel compromise
Treating the isolated Rust harness as a shipping backend
Designing a permanent backend abstraction or runtime selector

architecture_states.description: The shipping product uses matrix-js-sdk only. The WebView and service worker still participate in token and media handling.
architecture_states.security_posture: temporary pre-cutover exposure; risks remain open

architecture_states.description: Rust SDK foundation and disposable-Synapse probes are test-only and are not registered as a product Matrix backend.
architecture_states.security_posture: must use isolated accounts/processes and must not share a product token or device ID

architecture_states.description: One Rust supervisor owns the Matrix client, credentials, stores, sync, crypto, media, and lifecycle; the WebView receives bounded Synara-owned DTOs only.
Rollback uses a prior product build and intentionally retained inert legacy data; it is not an in-app runtime choice.
A production JS and Rust client run concurrently, share identity/session state, or are selected at runtime.

controls_required: typed bounded payloads and presentation DTOs
no long-lived session token, store key, recovery key, raw push payload, or decrypted media bytes
ephemeral login password or one-time token only in a one-shot inbound authentication command and never echoed, logged, or persisted
bounded sanitized event/presentation plaintext only on outbound rendering topics and never in diagnostics
opaque bounded media handles instead of media bytes
no raw SDK errors or identifiers

trust_boundaries.to: OS notification service and lock screen
controls_required: typed bounded notification DTO and IPC command
encrypted-room, private-mode, and lock-screen redaction policy
packaged platform and negative notification fixtures

threat_actors: malicious Matrix sender or room participant
same-user local process or filesystem attacker
stale asynchronous task from a superseded session generation
crash, power loss, disk error, or credential-store failure
malicious proxy configuration or credential-bearing URL
compromised dependency, build input, or CI artifact
operator or support recipient with diagnostic access

security_invariants.rule: Exactly one Rust Matrix client owner exists after cutover; no production backend selector or dual client is permitted.

No long-lived Matrix session token, store key, recovery key, raw push payload, or decrypted media bytes cross post-cutover WebView IPC or enter logs. An ephemeral login password or one-time login token may cross WebView-to-Rust only through a purpose-specific one-shot typed and bounded authentication command and is never echoed, logged, or persisted. Bounded sanitized event/presentation plaintext may cross Rust-to-WebView only on allowlisted rendering topics and never enters diagnostics; media uses opaque bounded handles rather than bytes.
The old token or device ID is not copied into a fresh Rust store without a separately approved continuity threat review.
A store is opened only with its matching account-scoped native secret; existing encrypted data plus a missing key is a recoverable error, not a new-key event.
Paths are absolute, canonical or safely rooted, symlink resistant, collision resistant, account isolated, and deleted only by exact idempotent operations.
New work is rejected and tasks are cancelled and joined before clients/stores close, credentials clear, or files are deleted.
IPC uses cross-language-safe counters, one authoritative stream identity, typed bounded bodies, stale-generation rejection, and bounded queues.
Media bytes do not travel as JSON; authenticated retrieval, decryption, cache bounds, metadata validation, revocation, and persistence policy are Rust owned.
A crash or partial migration never triggers automatic wipe and leaves legacy data inert and recoverable until an exact approved cleanup.
Widgets and calls cannot retain matrix-js-sdk as a hidden exception and must pass an explicit CSP/origin and experimental-feature review.

threats.scenario: Credentials remain in WebView/localStorage/service-worker memory, cross IPC, or are copied into the Rust session without a continuity review; a WebView fallback when native persistence is unavailable and session-scoped or unsupported platform stores can blur secure restore, fallback exposure, and durability; an authentication callback token can remain in URL/history-visible state or be accepted without complete origin, replay, state, nonce, and PKCE integrity checks.
required_controls: no credential-bearing WebView fallback after cutover
explicit per-platform persistence and recovery policy
clean-quit, crash, and OS-restart restore-or-reauthentication tests
consume-once callback token with pre-async URL/history scrub
strict callback origin and replay/malformed rejection
OAuth/OIDC state, nonce, and PKCE validation
hash-router, history-router, and hostile callback tests

threats.scenario: A missing, replaced, leaked, or partially deleted key strands or exposes an encrypted store; swallowed credential-store or Matrix IndexedDB deletion failures can leave retained state while logout appears complete.
required_controls: verified fail-closed credential and store deletion

threats.scenario: Traversal, symlink substitution, collision, or TOCTOU redirects creation or deletion outside the account root.
Unsafe integers, sequence overflow, stream-ID disagreement, unbounded JSON, or stale tasks corrupt state or leak sensitive payloads.
Untrusted media metadata/content, authenticated URLs, decrypted bytes, or object handles cause disclosure, resource exhaustion, unsafe file behavior, or persistence.
Raw SDK failures, URLs, identifiers, paths, content, or secrets enter errors, logs, health snapshots, or support exports.

Logout or wipe destroys files/keys while a client or task is live, or a partial failure leaves an indeterminate state; swallowed deletion errors can falsely report completion and reload without a visible recovery path.
required_controls: verified deletion with no completion or reload on failure

threats.scenario: Concurrent owners, reused device identity, premature cleanup, or an ambiguous cutover marker causes duplicated actions or data/identity loss.
An in-app selector or uncontrolled downgrade reopens legacy data while Rust is active or extends legacy credential exposure indefinitely.

Widget/call origins, CSP, experimental APIs, or a hidden JS SDK exception can expose credentials/content or defeat full replacement; mismatched listener identities can retain disposed call/widget state and process post-dispose events.
Credential-bearing or malformed proxy/homeserver URLs leak through configuration or raw SDK errors, or broaden network access.
Toolchain drift, unstable experimental features, unsupported native keyring behavior, or unvalidated platform packaging invalidates security assumptions.

Malformed/custom events lose necessary raw content or inject oversized/unsafe content across DTO and rendering boundaries; forwarding may also republish encrypted wire metadata or decryption-failure placeholders when it does not require successful clear content and an approved event type.
UIA, registration, search, or migration gaps lead to unsafe fallbacks or concealed JS SDK retention.
Over-broad Tauri commands or capabilities expose Matrix lifecycle, filesystem, or secret operations to untrusted WebView code.
Stale plans, agent drift, branch divergence, or artifact-only completion claims allow unresolved security defects through a gate.
Notification privacy metadata is lost before the native/OS boundary, or encrypted/private content and approval command previews reach OS notification or lock-screen surfaces.
required_controls: bounded notification DTO and IPC schema
packaged platform tests and negative IPC/OS fixtures

unresolved_decisions.safe_default: Retain inert data until the later of 30 days or two releases; do not clean automatically without the approved rule.

unresolved_decisions.decision: Cutover marker schema, privacy, permissions, and account identifier
unresolved_decisions.safe_default: No raw user ID; use a collision-resistant versioned account identifier and restrictive permissions.

unresolved_decisions.decision: Repair or discard behavior for an incomplete Rust store
unresolved_decisions.safe_default: Stop with recoverable error; preserve all data and never auto-wipe.

unresolved_decisions.decision: Behavior when Linux Secret Service is unavailable
unresolved_decisions.safe_default: Block persistent session completion; do not fall back to localStorage, files, or session-scoped keyutils.

unresolved_decisions.decision: Native media delivery and decrypted persistence policy
unresolved_decisions.safe_default: No WebView byte JSON and no durable decrypted persistence.

unresolved_decisions.decision: Whether pseudonymous stable identifiers are permitted in diagnostics
unresolved_decisions.safe_default: No stable account identifier until explicitly approved.

unresolved_decisions.decision: experimental-widgets feature use and exit criteria
unresolved_decisions.safe_default: Do not enable in production without explicit Phase 10 risk approval.
Prior-build rollback only, time-bounded, with no concurrently active Rust session.

acceptance.r0_2_effect: Documents threats, assigns risks, and makes decisions explicit; it closes no technical risk.
acceptance.phase_0_gate_effect: none; Phase 0 remains open until R0.8 formal acceptance
